slides.title: Call 1930 immediately
slides.body: The National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 can help flag the transaction quickly. Reporting early improves the chance of stopping the money.

slides.title: Complain at cybercrime.gov.in
slides.body: File a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. Keep screenshots, transaction IDs and the scammer's number ready.

slides.title: No such thing as 'digital arrest'
slides.body: Police, CBI or ED do not arrest people over video calls. Report suspicious calls and messages on Sanchar Saathi's Chakshu.
slides.hi: वीडियो कॉल पर गिरफ़्तारी नहीं होती

caption_linkedin:
Online fraud moves fast, and so should the response. If you or someone you know loses money to a cyber scam in India:

• Call the National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 as soon as possible — early reporting improves the chance of the money being stopped
• File a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal: cybercrime.gov.in
• Inform your bank immediately
• Remember: police, CBI or ED do not arrest people over video calls — so-called 'digital arrest' is a scam
• Suspicious calls and messages can be reported on Sanchar Saathi's Chakshu facility

If you need guidance on next steps after a fraud, you can consult a Bar Council-verified advocate on AdvocateSetu: https://advocatesetu.com

For general awareness only. Not legal advice.
